title: Default arguments
recap: Default arguments supply omitted trailing call arguments; they do not create extra overloads. Once a parameter has a default, later parameters in that declaration must also have defaults.
Defaults belong where callers can see them and should not be repeated across declarations and definitions. Callers can override earlier defaults only by supplying the needed preceding arguments.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement shippingCost(distance, packages, rate). Return distance*packages*rate, or -1 if distance < 0, packages < 1, or rate < 0. Add defaults so packages is 1 and rate is 2 when omitted. The stub deliberately has no defaults yet: adding the defaults is part of the exercise. All tested products fit int.
hints: Add = 1 to packages and = 2 to rate in the visible function signature.
Validate the fully supplied values inside the body.
